title: Measure the fixed cost of an mmseqs align call and cut the iteration count
body:
On the mgy run, progressive seeding ran 12 align iterations costing 2.5 to 4.0 s each with no trend, while n_take doubled each iteration and the active set shrank. Work per iteration should swing by an order of magnitude across twelve rounds, so a flat cost points to a fixed price per mmseqs align invocation, most plausibly loading the target db and prefilter db, with the alignment itself a small fraction.

First measure: run mmseqs align once on an empty or one-record prefilter db against the same target db. If the fixed cost is around 2.5 s, then 30 of the 36 s is startup twelve times over, and fewer iterations (a larger --prog-n, or a growth factor above 2) halve or quarter it with the same seeds out, since the active-set logic is unchanged. Ceiling: 36 s to roughly 10 s, 5% of the run, more than the two serial fixes together.

Not blocked on the libsail evaluation; it touches seed_stage.rs and the prog parameters only.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/2aff5e6c
notes.text: Measured 2026-10-08 on the 16-core box at 4 threads. Caveat: mmseqs here is an aarch64 binary run through qemu-aarch64-static, so absolute times are inflated by an unknown factor; ratios hold. Fixed cost per mmseqs align call, measured with an empty prefilter db: 68 ms wall against 100k targets, 240 ms against a 2,455,940-record db built from mgy.0001.fa. A slice with all 20,795 query records present but every record empty (what the slice writes for Terminated queries) costs 95 ms, so empty records are free too. Against the 100k leftover run's own six per-iteration slices, wall time tracks alignments calculated: 4.15M aln 73.8 s, 3.65M 49.5 s, 515k 8.9 s, 249k 5.3 s, 81k 2.6 s, 21.5k 1.7 s. 20,795 synthetic random pairs cost 0.53 s, so real candidates cost 2 to 3 times more per alignment than quick rejects. Conclusion: the startup hypothesis is refuted; the flat 2.5 to 4 s per iteration on the mgy run is alignment work. The likely reason it is flat is that n_take doubles while the active set roughly halves, so alignments per iteration stay near constant, and later iterations align deeper candidates of the queries with the most hits. Fewer iterations would not cut it and would likely add alignments. Verifying the flat-work reading needs per-iteration alignment counts from the 48-thread box; mmseqs prints 'N alignments calculated' per call, which nail discards. Scripts and outputs are in tmp-claude/2026-10-08-align-fixed-cost.
